\begin{tablenotes}\footnotesize
\item Pairs: target-context/donor-country pairs that share at least 10 products (counted over all interactions of both contexts) and for which the outcome is defined. Outcomes are centred within each target context, averaged to ordered country pairs, and correlated (Pearson) with the distance; two-sided $p$ from all 5,040 relabellings of the 7 countries (the distance matrix is relabelled; each ordered country pair keeps its own outcome and set of categories). Ratios: foreign/local agreement as in Table~\ref{tab:travel}, pairs with non-positive local agreement excluded. Gain: NDCG@10 of ItemKNN trained on local data plus all same-category data of one foreign country, minus local data only; random split; hyperparameters retuned on validation users in both arms (median gain over the 321 pairs +0.0005, 95\% CI [-0.0010, +0.0033]). Hofstede distance: Kogut--Singh index over six dimensions; shared language: the countries share an official language; geographic distance: great-circle distance between capitals (Supplementary Table S4). The first five rows are the 15 pre-specified tests: 1 of 15 with $p<0.05$, 0 below the Bonferroni threshold ($\alpha=0.05/15$). $^{a}$ Sensitivity row: IN Arts \& Crafts, whose local-only ItemKNN scores below chance, retained. Because several countries are interchangeable on a distance, the smallest attainable $p$ is 1/5040 for Hofstede, 12/5040 for language and 1/5040 for geography.
